questions.question_text: A box holds $50$ pencils. $\frac{3}{5}$ are blue. How many are blue?

options.why: This finds one fifth but does not take three fifths.
This subtracts the numerator from the quantity.

questions.question_text: A $72$ m trail is $\frac{5}{8}$ complete. How many metres remain?

options.why: This gives the completed distance rather than the remaining distance.

questions.question_text: A $\$60$ item is reduced by $\frac{1}{4}$ of its price. What is the sale price?

options.why: This gives the discount rather than the sale price.
This subtracts the denominator as dollars.

questions.question_text: A $7$ kg parcel is $\frac{3}{5}$ packing material. What mass is packing material?

options.why: This multiplies by three without dividing by five.

questions.question_text: A tank has capacity $200$ L and is $\frac{3}{4}$ full. Then $\frac{1}{5}$ of the water is used. How much remains?

options.why: This subtracts one fifth of the full capacity instead of the water present.
This gives the initial water and ignores the amount used.
This gives the amount used rather than the remainder.

questions.question_text: A student finds $\frac{4}{10}$ of $85$ tickets as $8\times4=32$. What correction is needed?

options.text: Round 8.5 down to 8, so 32 is exact.
options.why: Rounding changes the quantity and loses two tickets.
This does not divide the whole into tenths first.
